question: What is the difference in the number of years between the summer and winter Olympic events?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Since 1994, the Summer and Winter Olympic Games have been staggered so that each is held once every four years, but offset from each other by two years. (ओलंपिक खेल — ग्रीष्मकालीन और शीतकालीन)

 

• Until 1992 (Albertville Winter Games), both the Summer and Winter Olympics were held in the same calendar year. From 1994 (Lillehammer) onward, the Winter Games were shifted to fall exactly midway between two Summer Games.

 

• For example, the Tokyo Summer Olympics (2021) were followed 2 years later by the Beijing Winter Olympics (2022), which in turn were followed 2 years later by the Paris Summer Olympics (2024).

 

• Thus, a Winter Olympics always falls 2 years before or after the nearest Summer Olympics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Winter Olympics were first held in 1924 at Chamonix, France.

 

• Both the Summer and Winter Games individually follow a 4-year (quadrennial) cycle among themselves.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (1): Incorrect; the actual gap between the two events is 2 years, not 1.

 

• Option 3 (4): Incorrect; 4 years is the interval between two successive editions of the *same* Games (Summer-to-Summer or Winter-to-Winter), not between the two different events.

 

• Option 4 (3): Incorrect; this does not match the staggered 2-year gap adopted since 1994.

question: Battle of Plassey was fought between English company and Nawab of Bengal in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1757.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between the British East India Company, led by Robert Clive, and the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah. (प्लासी का युद्ध — 1757)

 

• It was fought at Plassey (Palashi), on the banks of the Bhagirathi River, in present-day West Bengal.

 

• Siraj-ud-Daulah's defeat was engineered largely through the treachery of his own commander-in-chief, Mir Jafar, who had secretly conspired with the British.

 

• This victory laid the foundation of British political power in India and led to Mir Jafar being installed as a puppet Nawab of Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The subsequent Battle of Buxar (1764) further consolidated British control and led to the grant of Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha to the Company in 1765.

 

• Robert Clive later became the first British Governor of Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (1750): Incorrect; no major event of this significance occurred in this year.

 

• Option 3 (1850): Incorrect; too late, British rule in Bengal was already well established by then.

 

• Option 4 (1857): Incorrect; this is the year of the Indian Rebellion/First War of Independence, not the Battle of Plassey.

question: Which of the following countries hosted the 2022 Asian Wresting Championships where Ravi Dahiya became the first Indian freestyle wrestler to win a hat-trick of gold medals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 Asian Wrestling Championships were held in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, in April 2022. (एशियाई कुश्ती चैंपियनशिप 2022 — उलानबातर, मंगोलिया)

 

• Indian wrestler Ravi Dahiya won gold in the men's freestyle 57 kg category, making it his third consecutive Asian Championship gold.

 

• With this win, he became the first Indian freestyle wrestler to win a hat-trick of gold medals at the Asian Wrestling Championships.

 

• Fellow Indian wrestler Bajrang Punia won a silver medal at the same edition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ravi Dahiya is also an Olympic silver medallist (Tokyo 2020, men's freestyle 57 kg).

 

• The Asian Wrestling Championships is organised annually by the United World Wrestling (UWW) - Asia body.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Almaty, Kazakhstan): Incorrect; this was the venue of an earlier edition of the Asian Wrestling Championships, not 2022.

 

• Option 2 (New Delhi, India): Incorrect; New Delhi hosted an earlier (2021) edition, not the 2022 one.

 

• Option 4 (Xi'an, China): Incorrect; Xi'an hosted the 2019 edition of the Championships.

question: In April 2022, ‘SVANidhi se Samriddhi’ program was launched in additional 126 cities. This program provides ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is social security benefits.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'SVANidhi se Samriddhi' is a saturation-based programme launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) to extend the benefits of various social security and welfare schemes of the Central and State Governments to street vendors covered under PM SVANidhi and their families. (स्वनिधि से समृद्धि — सामाजिक सुरक्षा लाभ)

 

• In April 2022, the programme was expanded/launched in an additional 126 cities, taking its total coverage to 222 cities across 26 States/UTs.

 

• It maps street vendors and their household members to schemes such as PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, PM Suraksha Bima Yojana, Ayushman Bharat, ration cards, etc.—providing them a wider social security net.

 

• The parent scheme, PM SVANidhi (PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi), was launched in June 2020 to provide affordable working-capital loans to street vendors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• PM SVANidhi offers vendors an initial working capital loan of up to ₹10,000, repayable in monthly instalments, with subsequent higher-value loans on timely repayment.

 

• The scheme also encourages digital transactions among street vendors through cashback incentives.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (insurance cover): Incorrect; insurance is only one component covered under the broader social security umbrella, not the defining purpose of the programme.

 

• Option 2 (scholarships to students): Incorrect; the programme is not targeted at student scholarships.

 

• Option 3 (hospital facilities): Incorrect; while health scheme linkage (Ayushman Bharat) is included, the programme's overall scope is social security, not hospital facilities per se.

question: In which of the following state of India, coniferous trees are found?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Coniferous (needle-leaf) forests, such as chir pine, deodar, blue pine and fir, are found in the Himalayan region at higher altitudes (roughly 1,500 m to 3,000 m). (शंकुधारी वन — उत्तराखंड)

 

• Uttarakhand, lying in the Himalayan belt, has extensive montane coniferous forests, particularly in districts like Nainital, Almora, Chamoli and Pithoragarh.

 

• These forests are adapted to cold, dry climates and are characterised by cone-bearing, evergreen trees with needle-shaped leaves.

 

• The other three states listed — Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh — are largely plains/plateau states and lack the high-altitude Himalayan terrain needed for coniferous forest growth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's coniferous forests are also found in Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.

 

• Coniferous forests are part of India's montane forest classification, distinct from tropical, deciduous and mangrove forest types.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (Bihar): Incorrect; Bihar is a plains state with tropical/sub-tropical vegetation, not coniferous forests.

 

• Option 3 (Uttar Pradesh): Incorrect; UP is predominantly a Gangetic plains state without high-altitude coniferous cover.

 

• Option 4 (Madhya Pradesh): Incorrect; MP has tropical deciduous forests, not coniferous ones.

question:
Which of the following is natural acid-base indicator?

I. Litmus

II. Turmeric
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Natural acid-base indicators are substances derived from plants that change colour depending on whether a solution is acidic or basic. (प्राकृतिक अम्ल-क्षार सूचक — लिटमस और हल्दी)

 

• Litmus, extracted from lichens, turns red in acidic solutions and blue in basic (alkaline) solutions — it is the most commonly used natural indicator.

 

• Turmeric, which contains the pigment curcumin, is yellow in neutral/acidic conditions but turns red/reddish-brown in basic solutions (this is why a soap/base stain on a turmeric-stained cloth often turns reddish).

 

• Since both litmus and turmeric independently exhibit distinct, characteristic colour changes with acids and bases, both qualify as natural acid-base indicators.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other natural indicators include red cabbage extract, China rose (Hibiscus) petal extract, and grape juice.

 

• Synthetic indicators include phenolphthalein and methyl orange, which are man-made chemical dyes rather than plant extracts.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Only II): Incorrect; it wrongly excludes litmus, which is also a natural indicator.

 

• Option 2 (Only I): Incorrect; it wrongly excludes turmeric, which is also a natural indicator.

 

• Option 3 (Neither I nor II): Incorrect; both litmus and turmeric are, in fact, natural indicators.

question:
Which of the following objectives of NAMASTE scheme launched by the centre in August 2022 is correct?

I. Zero fatalities in sanitation work in India

II. Sanitation workers are collectivized into SHGs and are empowered to run sanitation enterprises
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanized Sanitation Ecosystem) was launched in August 2022 jointly by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. (नमस्ते योजना — स्वच्छता कर्मी सुरक्षा)

 

• Statement I is correct: One of NAMASTE's core objectives is to achieve zero fatalities in sanitation work in India by ensuring no sanitation worker comes into direct contact with human faecal matter, through mechanisation.

 

• Statement II is correct: The scheme also aims to collectivise sanitation workers into Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and empower them to become entrepreneurs running sanitation-related enterprises, along with access to sanitation-related livelihood assistance schemes.

 

• NAMASTE succeeds the earlier National Action Plan for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) framework aimed at eliminating manual scavenging.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NAMASTE also seeks to provide occupational safety training, PPE kits, and health insurance coverage to sanitation and sewer workers.

 

• It builds on the Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers (SRMS), which it eventually aims to replace.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (Only II): Incorrect; it wrongly excludes Statement I, which is also a genuine objective.

 

• Option 3 (Only I): Incorrect; it wrongly excludes Statement II, which is also a genuine objective.

 

• Option 4 (Neither I nor II): Incorrect; both statements correctly describe objectives of the NAMASTE scheme.

question: Who among the following was the first Indian female musician to win the Grammy award?
solution_text:
The correct answer, as marked in the source answer key, is Shweta Pandit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The question asks about the first Indian female musician to win a Grammy Award. (ग्रैमी पुरस्कार — पहली भारतीय महिला संगीतकार)

 

• Among the options, Shweta Pandit is a well-known Indian playback singer who has been associated with several Bollywood films and independent music projects.

 

• The Grammy Awards are presented annually by the Recording Academy (USA) to recognise outstanding achievement in the music industry across numerous categories.

 

• Per the officially marked answer key of this paper, Option 3 (Shweta Pandit) is recorded as the correct response.

 

Therefore, as per the source answer key, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Grammy Awards were first presented in 1959 and are considered one of the most prestigious honours in the global music industry.

 

• Several Indian musicians, including A.R. Rahman, have won Grammy Awards for their contributions to film scores and world music.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Neeti Mohan): Not credited as a Grammy winner.

 

• Option 2 (Tanvi Shah): Not selected as the marked answer in this paper's key; however, independent verification shows Tanvi Shah won the Grammy for Best Song Written for a Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media for her rap portion in 'Jai Ho' (from *Slumdog Millionaire*, 2009), alongside A.R. Rahman and Gulzar, at the 52nd Grammy Awards (2010) — making her the widely credited first Indian woman to win a Grammy. See the flagged note in the corrections section.

 

• Option 4 (Shalmali Kholgade): Not credited as a Grammy winner.

question: According to census 2011, number of literates in India is ______ million.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 763.5.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India, 2011, the total number of literates in the country stood at approximately 763.5 million (763,498,517 persons). (जनगणना 2011 — साक्षर जनसंख्या)

 

• The overall literacy rate in 2011 was recorded at 74.04%, up from 64.83% in the 2001 Census.

 

• Male literacy stood at 82.14% and female literacy at 65.46%, reflecting the persistent gender gap.

 

• Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate among states (93.91%), while Bihar recorded the lowest (61.80%).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2011 Census was the 15th Census of India and the 7th after Independence, conducted under the Census Act, 1948.

 

• India's total population as per the 2011 Census was approximately 121 crore (1.21 billion).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (767.5):, Option 2 (765.5): and Option 3 (769.5): are all incorrect; they are close but do not match the officially recorded figure of 763.5 million literates.

question: Identify the function of plasmid DNA.
option_1: None of the given options are correct
option_3: To confer certain unique phenotypic characters to bacteria
option_4: To help in the formation of rRNA
solution_text:
The correct answer is To confer certain unique phenotypic characters to bacteria.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A plasmid is a small, circular, double-stranded, extra-chromosomal DNA molecule found mainly in bacteria, capable of replicating independently of the main chromosomal DNA. (प्लाज्मिड डीएनए — जीवाणु में विशेष लक्षण)

 

• Plasmids often carry genes that confer special/unique phenotypic traits on the bacterium, such as antibiotic resistance, resistance to heavy metals, or the ability to produce toxins.

 

• Because plasmids are not essential for the bacterium's basic survival but provide selective advantages under specific conditions, they are widely exploited in genetic engineering as vectors to carry and clone foreign genes.

 

• The pBR322 plasmid is a classic example used extensively as a cloning vector in recombinant DNA technology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plasmids replicate autonomously using their own origin of replication (ori).

 

• They are a key tool in biotechnology, enabling the insertion of genes of interest into host bacterial cells (e.g., production of human insulin in genetically engineered *E. coli*).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (None of the given options are correct): Incorrect; Option 3 correctly describes a genuine function of plasmid DNA.

 

• Option 2 (To form blood cells): Incorrect; blood cell formation (haematopoiesis) is a function of animal bone marrow, unrelated to bacterial plasmids.

 

• Option 4 (To help in the formation of rRNA): Incorrect; rRNA synthesis occurs via transcription of ribosomal RNA genes, not via plasmid function.

question: When, for the first time, did the Election Commission of India become a multi-member body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1989.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Election Commission of India (ECI) was originally a single-member body from its establishment on 25 January 1950 until 1989. (चुनाव आयोग — बहु-सदस्यीय निकाय 1989)

 

• It first became a multi-member body on 16 October 1989, when the President appointed two additional Election Commissioners along with the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), ahead of the 1989 general elections.

 

• However, these two additional posts were abolished on 1 January 1990, reverting the ECI to a single-member body.

 

• The ECI was again made a three-member body from 1 October 1993, and has continued as a multi-member body ever since, functioning on the principle of collective/majority decision-making.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The current composition (Chief Election Commissioner + 2 Election Commissioners) is governed by the Election Commissioners (Conditions of Service) Act, 1991 and, since 2023, also by the CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

 

• The ECI derives its authority from Article 324 of the Constitution of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (1995):, Option 2 (1985): and Option 4 (1994): are incorrect; none of these years mark the ECI's first transition to a multi-member body — that first occurred in 1989.

question: Krishna III of Manyakheta belonged to which dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rashtrakuta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Krishna III was one of the most powerful rulers of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, ruling from his capital Manyakheta (Malkhed) in present-day Karnataka, from around 939 CE to 967 CE. (कृष्ण तृतीय — राष्ट्रकूट वंश)

 

• He is remembered for his military campaigns into South India, notably defeating the Chola king Parantaka I at the Battle of Takkolam (949 CE), and briefly extending Rashtrakuta influence up to Rameswaram.

 

• Manyakheta served as the imperial capital of the Rashtrakuta dynasty from the reign of Amoghavarsha I onward.

 

• The Rashtrakuta dynasty ruled large parts of the Deccan between the 8th and 10th centuries CE, with earlier notable rulers including Dantidurga, Krishna I (builder of the Kailasa Temple, Ellora) and Amoghavarsha I.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rashtrakutas were great patrons of art and literature; Amoghavarsha I authored the Kannada work Kavirajamarga.

 

• The dynasty was eventually overthrown by the Chalukyas of Kalyani (Western Chalukyas) under Tailapa II around 973 CE.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Chera): Incorrect; the Cheras were a Sangam-age and later dynasty of Kerala/Tamil region, unrelated to Manyakheta.

 

• Option 2 (Pala): Incorrect; the Palas ruled Bengal and Bihar, with Krishna III having no connection to this dynasty.

 

• Option 4 (Gurjara-Pratihara): Incorrect; this dynasty ruled northern/western India from Kannauj, distinct from the Rashtrakutas of Manyakheta.

question: Who among the following was the first recipient of the State annual award Nishagandhi Puraskaram from the Government of Kerala in 2013?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mrinalini Sarabhai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Nishagandhi Puraskaram is a state annual award instituted by the Government of Kerala, presented at the Nishagandhi Dance and Music Festival in Thiruvananthapuram, to honour lifetime contributions to Indian classical dance and music. (निशागांधी पुरस्कारम — मृणालिनी साराभाई)

 

• Renowned Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi exponent Mrinalini Sarabhai was conferred the first Nishagandhi Puraskaram by the Kerala government in 2013.

 

• Mrinalini Sarabhai founded the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad and was a recipient of the Padma Bhushan as well.

 

• The award, given by the Department of Tourism, Government of Kerala, has since been conferred annually on eminent classical performing artistes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Later recipients of the Nishagandhi Puraskaram have included veteran musicians and dancers such as Ilaiyaraaja.

 

• Mrinalini Sarabhai was the wife of scientist Vikram Sarabhai and mother of dancer Mallika Sarabhai.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Madhavi Mudgal): Incorrect; a noted Odissi dancer, but not the first recipient of this award.

 

• Option 2 (Shobana C Pillai): Incorrect; not recorded as the first recipient of the Nishagandhi Puraskaram.

 

• Option 3 (Uday Shankar): Incorrect; a pioneering dancer, but he passed away in 1977, well before this award's institution in 2013.

question: Which of the following dance forms did NOT originate in South India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sattriya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sattriya is a classical dance form that originated in Assam (Northeast India), not South India. (सत्रीय नृत्य — असम)

 

• It was introduced in the 15th century by the Vaishnavite saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardeva as part of the devotional practices within Assamese sattras (monasteries).

 

• Sattriya was accorded the status of a classical dance of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000, the most recent addition to that list at the time.

 

• In contrast, Kathakali and Bharatanatyam originated in Kerala and Tamil Nadu respectively, and Kuchipudi originated in Andhra Pradesh — all South Indian dance forms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's recognised classical dance forms also include Odissi (Odisha), Kathak (North India), Manipuri (Manipur) and Mohiniyattam (Kerala).

 

• Sattriya performances traditionally combine dance, drama and music within the sattra monastic tradition of Assam.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Kathakali): Incorrect as the answer to "NOT South India"; Kathakali originated in Kerala, South India.

 

• Option 2 (Kuchipudi): Incorrect as the answer; Kuchipudi originated in Andhra Pradesh, South India.

 

• Option 4 (Bharatanatyam): Incorrect as the answer; Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu, South India.

question: Who among the following won a Padma Vibhushan award in year 1971?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uday Shankar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Uday Shankar, the pioneering dancer and choreographer regarded as the father of modern Indian dance, was conferred the Padma Vibhushan in 1971 by the Government of India. (उदय शंकर — पद्म विभूषण 1971)

 

• He is credited with creating a new genre of dance blending Indian classical traditions with Western theatrical stagecraft, and founded the Uday Shankar India Culture Centre in Almora.

 

• The Padma Vibhushan is India's second-highest civilian award, conferred for exceptional and distinguished service in any field.

 

• Uday Shankar was the elder brother of the celebrated sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Awards (Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri) are announced annually on Republic Day.

 

• Uday Shankar had earlier also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship, the highest honour of the Akademi.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Rajee Narayan):, Option 2 (S Swaminathan): and Option 3 (Devjani Chaliha): are incorrect; none of these persons feature in the official 1971 Padma Vibhushan list.

question: The fundamental duty of a parent or guradian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of 6 and ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A(k) of the Indian Constitution, inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, lays down that it is the fundamental duty of every parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child, or as the case may be, ward between the age of 6 and 14 years. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — 6 से 14 वर्ष तक शिक्षा)

 

• This duty corresponds directly with Article 21A, also inserted by the 86th Amendment, which makes free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for all children in the 6-14 age group.

 

• This age bracket (6-14 years) is also reflected in the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.

 

• Article 51A(k) is the eleventh and last of the Fundamental Duties listed in Part IVA of the Constitution, and the only one addressed to parents/guardians rather than to citizens generally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The original 10 Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee; the 11th duty (51A(k)) was added later in 2002.

 

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, i.e., they are not enforceable by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (20):, Option 3 (18): and Option 4 (16): are incorrect; the constitutionally specified upper age limit under Article 51A(k) is 14 years, not 20, 18 or 16.

question: Which of the following is NOT associated with Aryabhata?
option_1: Stated that day and night were caused by the rotation of the earth on its axis.
option_2: Developed a scientific explanation for eclipses
option_3: Found a way of calculating the circumference of a circle
solution_text:
The correct answer is Spoke about elaborate surgical procedures.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aryabhata (476-550 CE) was an ancient Indian mathematician-astronomer, author of the Aryabhatiya, who made pioneering contributions to astronomy and mathematics. (आर्यभट — खगोलशास्त्री एवं गणितज्ञ)

 

• He correctly explained that the apparent daily motion of the sky is due to the rotation of the Earth on its own axis, and that day and night are caused by this rotation.

 

• He gave a correct scientific explanation for solar and lunar eclipses, attributing them to the shadows cast by the Earth and Moon, rather than to mythological causes like the demon Rahu.

 

• He also worked out methods to calculate the circumference of a circle and gave a remarkably accurate approximate value of pi (π ≈ 3.1416).

 

• Detailed descriptions of elaborate surgical procedures, instruments, and techniques are instead the hallmark of Sushruta, the ancient physician known as the father of Indian surgery, author of the Sushruta Samhita — not Aryabhata.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aryabhata is also credited with early work on the place-value system and concepts approaching zero in Indian mathematics.

 

• India's first satellite, launched in 1975, was named Aryabhata in his honour.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Incorrect as the answer; this is correctly associated with Aryabhata's astronomy.

 

• Option 2: Incorrect as the answer; Aryabhata is indeed credited with a scientific explanation of eclipses.

 

• Option 3: Incorrect as the answer; calculating the circumference/value of pi is a genuine contribution of Aryabhata.

question: The Sahara Desert is located in which of the following continent?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Africa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sahara Desert is located in North Africa, spanning across parts of countries such as Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Sudan and Tunisia. (सहारा मरुस्थल — अफ्रीका महाद्वीप)

 

• Covering an area of about 9.2 million square kilometres, it is the largest hot desert in the world and the third-largest desert overall (after the polar deserts of Antarctica and the Arctic).

 

• It stretches roughly from the Atlantic Ocean in the west to the Red Sea in the east.

 

• The desert experiences extreme temperature variations and is characterised by sand dunes (ergs), rocky plateaus (hamadas) and sparse oases.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major deserts include the Thar Desert (India/Pakistan), the Gobi Desert (Mongolia/China), and the Kalahari Desert (Southern Africa).

 

• The Sahara is bordered to the south by a semi-arid region called the Sahel.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (South America): Incorrect; South America's major desert is the Atacama Desert.

 

• Option 2 (North America): Incorrect; North America's deserts include the Mojave and Sonoran Deserts.

 

• Option 4 (Australia): Incorrect; Australia's major deserts include the Great Victoria Desert, distinct from the Sahara.

question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the institutional structure of rural banking?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Moneylenders.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The institutional structure of rural credit/banking in India refers to formal, regulated sources of finance, including Commercial Banks, Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), and the Cooperative Credit structure (including Land Development Banks). (ग्रामीण साख संस्थागत ढांचा — औपचारिक स्रोत)

 

• Moneylenders, on the other hand, are a classic example of a non-institutional (informal) source of rural credit, operating outside the regulatory framework of banking institutions such as the RBI or NABARD.

 

• Other non-institutional sources include relatives, traders, commission agents, and landlords.

 

• Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were established under the RRB Act, 1976, following the recommendations of the Narasimham Committee, specifically to serve rural credit needs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development), established in 1982, is the apex institution overseeing rural credit and development in India.

 

• The cooperative credit structure includes Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), District Central Cooperative Banks, and State Cooperative Banks for short/medium-term credit, along with Land Development Banks for long-term credit.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (Regional rural banks): Incorrect as the answer; RRBs are a genuine part of the formal institutional structure.

 

• Option 3 (Commercial banks): Incorrect as the answer; commercial banks are a core institutional credit source.

 

• Option 4 (Cooperative and land development banks): Incorrect as the answer; these are also part of the formal institutional rural credit structure.

question: Who among the following proposed the term ‘ecosystem’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is AG Tansely.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The term 'ecosystem' was coined in 1935 by the British botanist and ecologist Sir Arthur George Tansley (A.G. Tansley). (पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र — ए.जी. टैन्सले)

 

• Tansley defined the ecosystem as a basic ecological unit comprising the biotic community (living organisms) and its abiotic (physical) environment, interacting as a functional system.

 

• This concept became foundational to the modern field of ecosystem ecology, emphasising the flow of energy and cycling of nutrients between organisms and their environment.

 

• Tansley's work built upon earlier ideas about the interdependence of organisms and environment expressed by ecologists in the early 20th century.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Raymond Lindeman later contributed significantly to ecosystem ecology through his trophic-dynamic concept (1942), describing energy flow through food chains.

 

• The term 'ecological niche' is associated with Joseph Grinnell and later Charles Elton.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (Grinnel): Incorrect; Joseph Grinnell is known for the concept of ecological niche, not for coining 'ecosystem'.

 

• Option 3 (Lindeman): Incorrect; Raymond Lindeman is known for the trophic-dynamic concept of energy flow, not for coining the term.

 

• Option 4 (Turreson): Incorrect; Göte Turesson is known for work on ecotypes in plant ecology, not for coining 'ecosystem'.

question: How many anions surround a sodium ion in a crystal lattice of sodium chloride?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Six.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sodium chloride (NaCl) crystallises in a face-centred cubic (FCC) lattice arrangement, also called the rock-salt structure. (सोडियम क्लोराइड — 6:6 समन्वय संख्या)

 

• In this structure, each sodium ion (Na⁺) is surrounded by six chloride ions (Cl⁻), and likewise, each chloride ion is surrounded by six sodium ions.

 

• This is described as a 6:6 coordination number, i.e., both the cation and the anion each have a coordination number of 6, arranged octahedrally.

 

• This close-packed arrangement arises because the radius ratio of Na⁺ to Cl⁻ favours an octahedral (6-coordinate) packing geometry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• In contrast, caesium chloride (CsCl) has a body-centred cubic structure with an 8:8 coordination number, due to the larger size of the Cs⁺ ion.

 

• The coordination number in ionic crystals is largely governed by the radius ratio rule between the cation and anion.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (Eight): Incorrect; this corresponds to structures like CsCl, not NaCl.

 

• Option 3 (Seven): Incorrect; seven-fold coordination is not a typical/stable geometry in simple ionic lattices like NaCl.

 

• Option 4 (Nine): Incorrect; this does not correspond to the NaCl rock-salt structure.

question: The Balance of Payment Account of an economy is related to the ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is external sector.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Balance of Payments (BoP) is a systematic statement recording all economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world over a given period, typically a year. (भुगतान संतुलन — बाह्य क्षेत्र)

 

• It is a core component of a country's external sector, along with foreign exchange reserves, exchange rate management, and trade policy.

 

• The BoP account is divided into the Current Account (trade in goods/services, income, transfers) and the Capital Account (capital transfers, investments, loans).

 

• In India, the BoP statistics are compiled and published by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A BoP surplus occurs when a country's receipts from abroad exceed its payments, while a BoP deficit is the reverse situation.

 

• Foreign Exchange Reserves are used by the RBI, among other things, to manage BoP imbalances and maintain currency stability.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (agriculture sector): Incorrect; BoP relates to a country's external economic transactions, not specifically to agriculture.

 

• Option 3 (government sector): Incorrect; BoP is not confined to government transactions alone.

 

• Option 4 (private sector): Incorrect; BoP records transactions of the economy as a whole with the rest of the world, not just the private sector.

question: Identify the step that is NOT a part of decomposition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Soil erosion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Decomposition is the process by which detritivores and decomposers break down complex organic matter (detritus) into simpler inorganic substances. (अपघटन प्रक्रिया — मृदा अपरदन शामिल नहीं)

 

• The key steps of decomposition include fragmentation (breaking detritus into smaller particles), leaching (water-soluble nutrients percolating into the soil), catabolism (breakdown of complex organic molecules into simpler ones by microbial/fungal enzymes), and humification (accumulation of a dark, amorphous, resistant substance called humus).

 

• Soil erosion, which refers to the removal/displacement of the top layer of soil by wind, water, or other agents, is an entirely separate process related to land degradation, and is not a step in the decomposition of organic matter.

 

• The final stage of decomposition after humification is mineralisation, where humus is further degraded to release inorganic nutrients.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The rate of decomposition depends on factors such as the chemical composition of detritus and climatic conditions like temperature and soil moisture.

 

• Humus is highly resistant to microbial action and decomposes very slowly, serving as a reservoir of nutrients for plants.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Leaching): Incorrect as the answer; leaching is a genuine step of decomposition.

 

• Option 2 (Humification): Incorrect as the answer; humification is a genuine step of decomposition, leading to humus formation.

 

• Option 3 (Catabolism): Incorrect as the answer; catabolism (microbial breakdown of detritus) is a genuine step of decomposition.

question: Who among the following has launched the US Startup SETU programme?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Piyush Goyal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The US Startup SETU (Supporting Entrepreneurs in Transformation and Upskilling) programme was launched by Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal in San Francisco, USA. (यूएस स्टार्टअप सेतु — पीयूष गोयल)

 

• The programme was designed to connect Indian start-ups with US-based investors, mentors, and industry leaders, fostering cross-border collaboration and investment opportunities.

 

• It was launched as part of efforts to strengthen the India-US start-up ecosystem and support Indian entrepreneurs seeking to scale globally.

 

• Piyush Goyal has also been closely associated with India's flagship Startup India initiative in his capacity as Commerce and Industry Minister.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Startup India was launched by the Government of India in January 2016 to build a strong ecosystem for nurturing innovation and start-ups.

 

• India's DPIIT (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade) functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, headed by Piyush Goyal at the time.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Amit Shah): Incorrect; he holds the Home Affairs and Cooperation portfolios, unrelated to this launch.

 

• Option 2 (Yogi Adityanath): Incorrect; he is the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, not associated with this Union-level initiative.

 

• Option 3 (Nitin Gadkari): Incorrect; he holds the Road Transport and Highways portfolio, not associated with this launch.

question: Nagabhata was the king of which of the following dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pratihara.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nagabhata I was the founder of the Gurjara-Pratihara (Pratihara) dynasty in the mid-8th century CE, ruling from the region around Malwa/Avanti. (नागभट — प्रतिहार वंश)

 

• He is celebrated for successfully checking the advance of Arab invaders into India from Sindh in the 8th century.

 

• A later, more prominent ruler, Nagabhata II, further expanded Pratihara power, capturing Kannauj and making it the dynasty's capital.

 

• The Pratiharas were one of the three major powers of early medieval North India, engaged in the long Tripartite Struggle for control of Kannauj with the Palas of Bengal and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pratihara ruler Mihira Bhoja is regarded as one of the greatest kings of the dynasty, expanding the empire to its zenith.

 

• The Pratiharas patronised the construction of numerous temples in the Nagara style of temple architecture, particularly in and around Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Kakatiya): Incorrect; the Kakatiyas ruled the Telangana region, unrelated to Nagabhata.

 

• Option 2 (Vardhana): Incorrect; the Vardhana (Pushyabhuti) dynasty, whose most famous ruler was Harshavardhana, ruled from Thanesar/Kannauj but is a distinct lineage from the Pratiharas.

 

• Option 4 (Reddy): Incorrect; the Reddy dynasty ruled parts of the Andhra region in the 14th-15th centuries, much later and unrelated to Nagabhata.
